questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English as the first language, multiculturality, bigger city. On top of that, wanted to understand what American/Canadian culture is about.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university is great but the workload is way higher than at KU, students have to memorize quite a lot for exams and 90% of them are handwritten. The university has a lot to offer ranging from different clubs to the coolest sports center I've ever seen. This exchange could really be anything from a 1 to a 10, it all depends on how much effort you put in to socialize, as the university doesn't really arrange many events for you. The city has a lot of great food and cultural activities! In addition, it's really affordable to visit other cities in Canada

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy it's mostly on the website + the emails sent out are by UoT are rather informative, however, a lot of back-and-forths information emails with the inbound exchange office as the university is insanely strict about which courses you can take; course prerequisites are not flexible and if there is no overlap with their descriptions you can end up with no courses at all. In my case, it was fairly hard as I'm studying Social Data Science which is a new degree.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When the university is starting, there wasn't much information presented yet most of it could be found on the website. My advice is to get really familiar with the study portal. The university could have done a better job by creating guides for incoming exchange students, it took me a lot of time to find info on the website. Once again it stems down to how motivated you are to find the info.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Not many orientation events, most of them were booked out once I opened the emails. In my opinion, this shouldn't be the case, it doesn't make an inbound orientation activity limited in space. Your social life mostly depends on various events organized by other exchange students. Once again it is all in your hands, hence emphasizing that the experience of going to this exchange can vary a lot.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through a friend, otherwise, the university was very unhelpful. More specifically, the university prioritizes full-time students over exchange students for their on-campus housing. The rental market is the same, everybody wants students for at least 1 year. Without my friend, I would probably end up paying a fortune or in a remote location.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a hassle to find something, start your apartment hunt soon!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very satisfied, finding a place for 1-semester exchange students is not easy at all. You better start before the final decision of approval comes in!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience with course registration was the worst part of the whole exchange. My degree is fairly new, hence it was quite impossible to comply with the university prerequisites. For this reason, I didn't get any of my desired courses.  The exchange office is always willing to help, but the main decisions are in the departments' hands, hence some departments will just reject you right away. The foundation of this university is bureaucracy. Most departments don't understand that the courses in Denmark are not 100% identical to the courses in Canada and reject you based on that.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The system is rather outdated and takes a lot of time, they were using google forms instead of the normal registration process for exchange students, I submitted several of these forms and got into some courses in the last round

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write an email from Europe. Once you are there; you could call or book the inbound exchange office through zoom.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely unsuccessful and did not get (almost) any classes I wanted to take, there is no flexibility!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make your research about prerequisites and stick to them. The university is run by bureaucrats so they don't understand that people in Europe have a hard time getting exactly the same courses they have in prerequisites.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although I didn't get my desired courses, the level of education is rather high and I learned a lot. To be specific, the computer science courses are very well taught at the university, yet are way harder than the economics courses I took. The university puts a lot of assignments on your shoulders and it seems like students are usually overwhelmed. However, finishing such an intense semester can be rather rewarding.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As described above, the courses are tough yet rewarding, especially computer science.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is different, there are weekly assignments for most subjects, a mid-term exam, and a final exam. Some courses are taught in smaller classes. In contrast, the computer science course I took is taught in a large auditorium.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Databases
Special Topics in Economics with Data Analytics
Special Topics in Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to  Databases; Although it's the hardest course, you are learning a lot. It's the most useful course out of the three I took as it teaches how to design a database and use SQL. On top of that, the lectures are entertaining.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: CN tower was quite expensive, but if you go during sunset it's worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is less expensive, and mobile providers are more expensive. Public transport can be fairly cheap using city bikes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and extracurricular activities, this is what the university does right!! Though they should have a better system for informing students about these activities, I was a bit overwhelmed by the events happening around me.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Free gym center with a swimming pool. Free university sports events (as a spectator). Social activities by clubs,  there is a club for everyone!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: different clubs, everyone is into something else. I would recommend attending the club fair in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: CN tower, Toronto Islands, Niagara falls, NYC, Washington or any other cities in the US

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: fairly easy, it's very similar to Europe (and so is the metric system). Though there were a few cultural shocks (such as raccoons on the streets)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to bars, and university events. Just go out and talk to people. Canadians are one of the friendliest people!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: wild animals in the streets

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: friendliness and genuine interest of Canadians

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be ready to socialize and seek those events 
2. Make your weekly assignments, they can save your grade
3. Travel in your free time, really recommend NYC and Washington it's fairly closeby

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: nothing on top of my mind

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: traveling, meeting new people, studying

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: course selection, that period was insanely stressful, they should really be more transparent with their processes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
